hypotheses_validated.claim: MAJOR finding reproduced and fixed: with prefetch on, a failed hearth_eval left prefetch reads outstanding (issued/read/timed after it returned), and hints it had prefetched (hidden issue) were later used by the retry (prefetch_used > prefetch_issued). Now model.c records every (layer, expert) key handed to hx_store_prefetch with a state (HINT_NOW this call, HINT_PREV previous call, HINT_USED once a layer's union routes to it, which its own acquire settles); at the start of each call NOW becomes PREV and older/used entries are dropped; on failure drain_hints() does hx_store_acquire + hx_store_release on every NOW/PREV key before the store tick and before s1 is read, so no read the call (or the previous call) caused lands after it returns and its counts fall inside the hidden delta.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: New test_prefetch_failures part 1 (fresh engine, SHARED, extra INT_MAX, layer-2 reads 30 ms, failure at layer 1): unfixed code 'before: issued 0 ... after: issued 0 ... +300ms: issued 5, bytes 290816, read_s 0.244' (FAIL); fixed: counters equal at return and after 300 ms, store shows issued > 0 and used > 0 inside the call, retry bit-identical, used <= issued, hits + misses = uses. Part 2 (previous call's prefetch of an expert u it predicted but did not route to, u's read 200 ms; next call fails at layer 1 without predicting u): unfixed 'after B: issued 1 ... +300ms: issued 2, bytes 143360' (FAIL); fixed equal. hypotheses_validated.claim: A latent flaky test was fixed: test_prefetch_gate failed deterministically for some seeds (e.g. 121, also with the gen-001 code and test: '3 imprecise predictions still issued') because its 64-row random replay used only rows 0-23 every pass, and those 24 rows can match the router's predictions ~50% of the time, keeping the gate open. The layer-2 prediction does not depend on routing (it is taken before layer 1's routed experts are added), so the test now takes it from a clean run and replays rows that hit exactly one of the two predicted experts at even positions and none at odd ones (precision 25%).

hypotheses_falsified.claim: A GQA leak test (8 slots, even layer-1 experts failing) catches a missing release in the failing-layer drain.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: It did not (mutant passed 2111 checks): GQA has 8 experts per MoE layer, so at most its 4 readable layer-1 experts can leak and the 4 remaining slots still let every call progress. Moved to make_mla (16 experts, 10 slots) plus the explicit hold-every-slot check.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Draining each unresolved hint in two phases (try_acquire all, then wait) is needed to keep the failure path fast.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Not needed at measured costs (+2.4 ms at layer 1, +14 ms at layer 47 on the q30-shaped container); kept the simpler sequential acquire/release. Not measured on DeepSeek-class slabs (44 MB): estimated ~0.5-1 s extra per failed call there with a small cache (open question).

open_questions: Attention value pass (T08 finding / verifier minor 4) is still portable-C speed: needs the hx_kernels value_acc entry proposed in contract_issues (kernels owner), then value_sum calls it. Not changed this generation.

Prefetch hints from two or more calls back that are still queued when a call fails are not waited for (the store's prefetch queue holds at most max(2*top_k, 2*n_io) keys and is FIFO, so this needs prefetch reads starved by demand reads for a whole call). An hx_store quiesce/cancel API (contract_issues) would remove this and the extra reads.

Every expert a failed call waits for counts one use in the store (LFU heat, usage_out counts) because hx_store_acquire always counts a use; hints the store had dropped are read once. Caching only; output unaffected (INV-DET-1).
The failure path ticks the store once (from gen-001): usage_out's tokens_observed and LFU decay count a failed call as one token.
Failure-path cost on DeepSeek/Kimi-sized slabs (44 MB) with a small cache is estimated, not measured.
